Hi Sophie — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the friction. We recently had a few customers hit the same behavior: Calendly and Chili Piper usually detect the invitee's browser locale, but when a recipient has a different device or an OS that hasn't applied a DST update (or a VPN with a foreign location), the conversion can look wrong.

Quick answers / options:
1) I can send a manual calendar invite in UTC with the meeting time spelled out in CET/CEST and PST so there is no ambiguity.
2) Use the Calendly link with an explicit timezone parameter: https://calendly.com/redwood/demo?tz=Europe/Berlin — that forces the page to present Berlin times.
3) If you prefer Chili Piper, it has a known quirk where it sometimes honors the browser but not the calendar account timezone; we can include an ICS fallback.

Proposed slots (I'll keep these free on our side):
- Tue 2026-04-06 08:00 UTC (Tue 10:00 CEST) — 40 min
- Wed 2026-04-07 12:00 UTC (Wed 14:00 CEST) — 40 min
- Wed 2026-04-07 15:00 UTC (Wed 17:00 CEST) — 40 min (later option)

If any of those work I'll send the invite (and attach an .ics). If you'd rather us open a Calendly page set to Europe/Berlin and you rebook from there, that also works. Apologies again — we're tightening the scheduling flow to display UTC alongside local time.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks

Looping in to offer a small ops suggestion: when timezone confusion is likely (cross-region, DST around the corner), I usually include both a UTC timestamp and two local anchors in the invite body, e.g.:

"Tue 6 Apr · 08:00 UTC · 10:00 CEST · 02:00 PDT (same moment)"

Also recommend adding an ICS that contains the TZ definitions (some calendar clients ignore numeric offsets and instead map to a TZ ID; that helps preserve DST behavior). I'm attaching a generic fallback-times.ics file with Europe/Berlin explicitly set — you can attach it to the invite if Dylan sends one.

If Sophie prefers an open Calendly page, add the ?tz=Europe/Berlin param and include a short sentence: "If your calendar shows a different time, reply with your timezone or accept the UTC time above."

—Marissa
